body.statement: If \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\) and \(\delta<\beta\), then \(\sup_{z\in\mathcal Z_\eta}\lVert M^{+}\log\widetilde H(z)-\log G(z)\rVert_2\leq E_M\), \(\sup_{z\in\mathcal Z_\eta}\lVert\mathscr R_M(\widetilde H)(z)-G(z)\rVert_2\leq e^{E_M}E_M\), and \(\sup_{z\in\mathcal Z_\eta}\max_r|\mathscr R_M(\widetilde H)_r(z)/G_r(z)-1|\leq e^{E_M}-1\).
body.justification: The result separates qualitative rank from operational amplification through both \(\lVert M^{+}\rVert_2\) and pooled-PGF attenuation.
body.gap: Shih--Hero provides the high-level independent-additive transform-inversion precedent but does not supply this multivariate lower-envelope perturbation bound for designed count pools.
body.consumer: It screens compositions and grid locations before running the more expensive validated certificate.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(z\in\mathcal Z_\eta\).  Monotonicity of \(z^v\) in every coordinate gives
\[
G_r(z)\geq G_r(\eta,\ldots,\eta)=\gamma_r.
\]
Equation (9) then gives \(H_j(z)\geq\prod_r\gamma_r^{M_{jr}}\geq\beta\).  Since every coordinate error is at most its Euclidean norm,
\[
\widetilde H_j(z)\geq H_j(z)-\delta\geq\beta-\delta>0. \tag{17}
\]
The scalar mean-value theorem for the logarithm and (17) imply
\[
|\log\widetilde H_j(z)-\log H_j(z)|
\leq\frac{|\widetilde H_j(z)-H_j(z)|}{\beta-\delta}.
\]
Taking Euclidean norms and using the definition of \(\delta\) yields
\[
\|\log\widetilde H(z)-\log H(z)\|_2
\leq\frac{\delta}{\beta-\delta}. \tag{18}
\]
Under full column rank, the rank-frontier identity is
\(M^+\log H(z)=\log G(z)\).  Submultiplicativity applied to (18) proves
\[
\|M^+\log\widetilde H(z)-\log G(z)\|_2
\leq \|M^+\|_2\frac{\delta}{\beta-\delta}=E_M. \tag{19}
\]

Write \(\Delta=M^+\log\widetilde H-\log G\).  Since \(0<G_r\leq1\),
\[
|\exp(\log G_r+\Delta_r)-G_r|
=G_r|e^{\Delta_r}-1|
\leq e^{|\Delta_r|}|\Delta_r|
\leq e^{E_M}|\Delta_r|.
\]
Summing squares proves the second asserted bound.  Division by \(G_r>0\) gives
\[
\left|\frac{\mathscr R_M(\widetilde H)_r}{G_r}-1\right|
=|e^{\Delta_r}-1|
\leq e^{|\Delta_r|}-1\leq e^{E_M}-1.
\]
All bounds are independent of \(z\); taking the stated suprema completes the proof.
